comments.body: Need to look into `mkForce` behavior. (marking as draft)

I guess the expected behavior for mkForce would be something like:

```
x.a = "some value"
x.b = "value b"
x.a = lib.mkForce "new value"

x => [ { a = "new value" } { b = "value b"; } ] # not sure about order on this one 
```

```
x.a = "some value"
x.a = lib.mkForce "value a"
x.a = lib.mkForce "value b"

x => [ { a = "value a"; } { a = "value b"; } ]
```

```
x.b = "some value"
x = lib.mkForce [ { a = "new value"; } ]

x => [ { a = "new value"; } ]
```
the type feels pretty good to use now. I'm new to valueMeta, but it feels like it should also expose the order? I wasn't able to find out the current value for order at all.

For context, the `asAttrs = true` use case shifts the tradeoff so that these options are easier to use for end users, at a small cost to the implementation of the built-in module.

Having to retrieve the unadulterated list through `options.args.valueMeta.attrListValue` is a bit heavy, but in its default configuration (`asAttrs ? false`), that value is simply available in `config`, e.g. `config.args` if you were to adjust the example. (But then users can't retrieve values as easily, having to dig through the list or recombine it themselves.)

For a module that goes into the package modules concept, the tradeoff as presented in `example.nix` seems optimal for users, because the `valueMeta` detail is hidden from them. Both options will be documented.

@Lassulus The last two commits should help with that, giving you access to some generated definitions, and a function to transform them.

Example:
```nix
      config.process.argv = lib.modules.mapDefinitionValue (
        attr: lib.cli.toCommandLineGNU { } attr
      ) (lib.mkMerge options.process.flags.valueMeta.definitions);
```

I've also had to change your `argv` definitions to:
```nix
  config.process.argv = lib.mkMerge [
    [ "nix" ]
    (mkOrder 1100 [ "flake" ])
    (mkOrder 1101 [ "show" ])
  ];
```

Otherwise, `listOf` wouldn't pick up the ordering. This could perhaps be fixed too, in a separate PR.

Then only one issue remains: flags without explicit mkOrder default to priority 1000 (same as plain argv elements). If flags should generally sort after subcommands, users would need to use `mkBefore`/`mkAfter`/`mkOrder` explicitly.
*Maybe* something could be done by relying on module ordering (order of `evalModules` `modules`, submodule modules, `imports`, that kind of thing), but relying on that is a bit risky because of `reverseList`.
It might also make sense to pull out argv0 so that we can put `mkBefore` or something to that effect, so that users don't have to think about that, and `mkBefore` becomes the first argument, not the executable.

argv0 (or maybe we can call it executable or something more descriptive?) sounds like a good idea anyway, since it usually is special and accessing it at other places inside the module is nicer without doing builtins.head config.argv
thanks! I will try to work on the flags addition to modular services later this week, since this is now merged a rebase is probably enough

+
+    Definitions can be provided in two formats, which may be mixed via `lib.mkMerge`, `imports`, etc:
+
+    - **List format**: `[ { a = 1; } { b = 2; } ]` — each element must be a single-attribute attribute set.
+      Elements may be wrapped in `lib.mkOrder` (or `lib.mkBefore`/`lib.mkAfter`) to control ordering;
+      unwrapped elements use the default order priority.
+
+    - **Attribute set format**: `{ a = lib.mkOrder 100 1; b = 2; }` — each name-value pair becomes a single-attribute attribute set in the output.

reviews.body: rebased https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/509595 on top of this and played around with it. seems cool and do what needs to be done :)
IA this seems cool and I can see the endless usecases for this. 😆

Looks good to me overall useful for modelling cli arguments and ordered sets.

Two things i'd request to fix before merge

- type merging is broken
- documentation should provide an example

Approving after adding my suggestions.

Notably:

- Disable type merging: Its broken if the payload contains a non-comparable function.
  Not allowing type-merging should be fine for this type imho.
- Handle error cases for better debugging.
